svg.title: South Africa wine-growing study atlas
svg.desc: An enlarged Cape view separates the tightly clustered western wine districts without moving them across South Africa. Approximate study locations, not appellation boundaries. Numbers refer to the study key; a shared number connects places in one grouped lesson. 1: Swartland. North of Cape Town, around the Malmesbury and Riebeek landscape. 2: Stellenbosch. East of Cape Town and south of Paarl, close to False Bay. 3: Paarl. Northeast of Cape Town and north of Stellenbosch. 4: Franschhoek. An inland valley southeast of Paarl and east of Stellenbosch. 5: Constantia. On the Cape Peninsula immediately south of central Cape Town. 6: Elgin. An elevated basin southeast of Stellenbosch, inland from the coast. 7: Walker Bay / Hemel-en-Aarde. The southern coastal area near Hermanus; Hemel-en-Aarde lies inland of the bay. 8: Robertson. Inland in the Breede River landscape, east of the Cape Town–Stellenbosch cluster.

g.text: Dots locate representative places · boundaries do not represent appellations
